neighbours.label: the word just before 'toll' in the idiom 'take a/its/their toll' (anticipating 'toll')
fire: Decades of salt air and neglect have taken their toll on the old pier.
Working night shifts for years finally took its toll on her sleep.
Everyone agrees that the drought is taking a toll on local farmers.
Long commutes can take a heavy toll on family life.
The endless rain this spring took its toll on the vineyard.
Doctors warn that chronic loneliness takes a toll on the heart.
Three straight losses have clearly taken their toll on the team's morale.
The heat wave took a toll on the city's ageing power grid.
quiet: Decades of salt air and neglect have left the old pier in poor shape.
Working night shifts for years, she finally took a long holiday.
Everyone agrees that the drought is hurting local farmers badly.
Long commutes can take up most of the evening for parents.
The endless rain this spring kept the vineyard workers indoors.
Doctors suggest that patients take their time after surgery.
After three straight losses the team took a short break from training.
During the heat wave many residents took a seat in the shade.

notes: Card: top 32 peak on ' a'/' their'/' its'/' taken' right before ' toll'. Probe: 'taken their toll' 0.87, 'took its toll' 0.54, 'taken a walk' 0.03. Near misses use take/took with other objects (time, break, seat).
